quest.title: The Formula for a Miracle
quest.description: The boundary between medicine and poison seems to have blurred, as has the line between life and death... Where can one find a truly perfect remedy, or does it exist at all?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x675, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Gold x5, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Return to the west of Qingce Village

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Ugh... That strange feeling is back...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: It's just like the day I went missing... It's as if something inside me is trying to guide me somewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: The mother lode's influence is growing stronger... But is it because we're getting closer to the source, or because the leakage of Chi blood is growing more severe?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Jialiang, can you sense which direction the source is in?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: I think it's... this way!

talks.objective: Talk to Jialiang and the others

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hmm... There is an inauspicious presence here. Even I can sense it.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: I think I remember this place... Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jialiang! Are you okay? Maybe you should rest here while we continue the search?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: No... I have to keep going. Jiangli is still waiting for me...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Phew... Then let's hurry!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Hm? From the looks of it, you've already tracked down the location of the source?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've made some progress...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Really? That's good to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you been standing guard here this entire time?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...I cannot simply look the other way when evil spirits are involved.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: In any case, the evil presence here is growing stronger. I can sense it.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...Whatever you're planning to do, make it quick.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: If you leave it too long, and I am compelled to intervene... things may not turn out the way you wish.

talks.objective: Talk to Baizhu and the others

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh... This place gives Paimon the creeps. Who knows what we're gonna find up ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: The digging marks here appear amateur, and rather old... I suspect it is a thieves' tunnel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A thieves' tunnel? Hmm, Paimon has heard rumors about treasure around these parts before... Maybe it was the Treasure Hoarders that dug this tunnel?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Judging by the tools they left behind, it's certainly a possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...But why did they abandon this place without even stopping to pack up their tools?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: ...I remember now. She took me here once and told me that she'd found a way to save me in this cave...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: But she... She said that the method would cause me to... Ugh, curses, why can't I remember what she said? Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Easy, Jialiang. Come on, let's keep going.

talks.objective: Talk to Baizhu and the others

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there's a censer here... Those Treasure Hoarders sure made themselves at home...

choices.text: (I don't see any dust on the censer's surface...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I don't think this was left here by the Treasure Hoarders.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...I believe this censer was used to burn a monster-repelling incense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A monster-repelling incense? You sure? 'Cause we did run into that group of monsters just now.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: The incense was burned several days ago. If I had to guess, the monsters we fought just now were enticed here by some entity deeper inside the cave.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: No doubt an encounter with the very same entity was what prompted the Treasure Hoarders to flee and abandon their designs on this cave.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: After them, Jiangli was the next person to discover this place, and what lies inside... But to her, it presented an opportunity to save Jialiang's life, albeit as a last resort...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: That's right... This censer — it belongs to Jiangli! Yes, this was the place!

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: This is where... I told Jiangli to give me the poison... *cough* *cough*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jialiang!

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: I'm fine... Let's keep going. I can feel it, sh—she... is right below us... waiting for me.

choices.text: (The burn marks on the inside are still fresh...)

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Everyone, please be careful.

talks.objective: Talk to Baizhu and the others

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu, how serious is it? Is she...?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I can still feel a pulse, but her condition is quite grave.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: The god remains here are encroaching on her cognition, much as the poison in your system did to you.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: If we don't eliminate it soon, then even if we save her life... I fear that she may never wake up again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then what are we waiting for? Let's destroy the remains right away!

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: ...It's not as simple as that. Don't you remember what Baizhu said?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: The poison within Jialiang's body is inextricably linked to the god remains here.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: ...If the source is purged, the poison in his system will stop having any effect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... And the poison within Jialiang's body is keeping his heart condition under control. So, if it stops working...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no! Are you saying...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Indeed. If the god remains here are purged... then your life will come to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* I wondered when this day might come...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, wait, wait! But we've all been working our butts off to save Jialiang's life! After all that... we can't just give up on him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Baizhu, you're a great doctor, surely you've gotta know of some other way we can save him... right?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...You could continue to take the poison, which would buy you some time. As for Jiangli... Maybe if we put our heads together, we can think of something.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: It appears to me that she was striving to concoct your medicine for you, right up until the moment when she lost consciousness... Maybe it's her greatest wish that you will continue to take it, and live...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu, give it to me straight. ...How long does Jiangli have?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: The god remains have reached her internal organs. Under ordinary circumstances, I would give her less than three days. But if I were to treat her using a secret art...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...But what would be the point of that?

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Dr. Baizhu... I'm all too aware of the dangers of god remains. You are not the first to mention it to me.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: If I continue to sustain my own life using this wretched substance, not only would Jiangli have to keep risking her life to make my medicine for me, but I would have to live with the looming threat of these remains breaking out and wreaking havoc not just upon me, but my entire family...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...I know for a fact that I should have died over a decade ago. The fact that I've been around to see Ayu grow up is already a great blessing from Rex Lapis.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: If my choice can bring Jiangli back... then even if I... even if I... die...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jialiang...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...Hah, after cheating death for so long, it seems I've grown somewhat addicted to life.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Dr. Baizhu... Could I have another minute with my wife? I just want to have... one final moment together. Just a moment, that's all.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...Of course.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Thank you, everyone. And I'm sorry that... I won't be able to repay your kindness in this life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sniff* Jialiang... Baizhu, Changsheng, is there really nothing else you can do?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: I am sure that over the years, Jiangli will have tried all the conventional methods known to humankind. As for less-conventional methods, I have little expertise besides Changsheng's secret art...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Mortals are fated to grow old and pass on when their natural lifespan runs out. If it were so easy to combat the natural processes of aging and death, Jiangli would not have had to resort to unnatural methods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a crazy situation... Jiangli risked it all to save Jialiang's life, and now, Jialiang has to sacrifice himself to save Jiangli... Wh—What's the point of it all?

choices.text: All we can do right now...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: I've seen many final farewells in my time... but I can never get used to it.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: In the human realm, all things must come to an end... Is it not a fitting end to die for a worthy cause?

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...At least, that's what generations of masters before you have always believed.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: The path they chose was indeed a heroic one. But when I think of those who would willingly sacrifice themselves for others...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...I cannot help but think that theirs are the lives least deserving of death.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...When all this began, we agreed that once Ayu was old enough to help you gather herbs, it would be time for me to go...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: If you could only see him now... He took me all the way to Liyue Harbor to see the doctor, and he even got the Adventurers' Guild to search for you...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...So I know that you'll both be okay without me.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: I've said my goodbyes. My time has come... Do what you must.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: As you wish.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...Ugh... Arghhh...

response.speaker: Jiangli
response.text: ...It will eat away at both your cognition and your memories... In the end, you'll become little more than a shadow of your true self...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...I'll take it. At the very least... It will allow me to stay with you, and watch Ayu grow up.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...*pained breathing*...

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: ...Mom! Something's really wrong with Dad...

response.speaker: Jiangli
response.text: ...Don't fret, Ayu. I will gather some medicinal herbs right away. I promise you, nothing will happen to our family...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: *groans*... Why would these memories come to mind now...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: *sigh* ...The longer we live, the tighter we cling to what we have...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Oh, how I would love... to hear... to hear your voice one last time...

choices.text: Is honor Jialiang's decision and bear witness.
You can't be thinking about that again...

dialogues.text: ...Jialiang... Jialiang!

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Jialiang! Jialiang!

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dad! Are you awake?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Uh... Jiangli... Ayu?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: ...Didn't I... Hm? What are... these?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: How does it feel to come back to life?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Do you feel strange or different in any way? If so, could you describe it to me in detail?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu! I... I thought that I was going to...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hehe, die? You did indeed. As things stand now, you're more akin to a zombie than a human.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: ...I'm a zombie?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: That's right. Before we set off, I asked Qiqi to prepare an... Elixir of Immortality. With its help, you have been suspended in the space between life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Of course, this is but a crude imitation of an adeptus art. I don't expect it to extend your life indefinitely.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Whether it will keep you alive for a few days, a few months, or a few years... I am as interested as you to find out.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: But however long you have left, I believe it should be more than sufficient time for you to say your final goodbyes before departing the world in peace. ...I hope that Director Hu finds this arrangement to be a satisfactory one?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: An "Elixir of Immortality"? How'd you cook that up? Ugh, leave it to you to work on something like that behind my back...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: It's a work in progress that hardly lives up to its name. And it would have had no effect were it not for Jialiang's iron will.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: In the end, I am merely a doctor. I understand very little of the great principles governing life and death, and the perpetual cycle of yin and yang.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: All I know is that if I'm presented with a life that deserves to be saved, I will do everything in my power to save them.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: And even this would have counted for nothing without Director Hu's assistance... After all, did you not tell Jialiang to show us the way before we set off for Qingce Village?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oops, aaaand I'm busted.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Without Director Hu nudging things in the right direction, we may not have found Jiangli in time.

choices.text: I KNEW someone was listening in on that conversation...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: No wonder he didn't mention the elixir back then. Hmph, I thought he was being frank and transparent with me for once, but apparently not...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Ahem... Hehe, Director Hu told me to keep her suggestion a secret. But it seems nothing escapes Dr. Baizhu's attention.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Hehehe, never underestimate a serpent's sense of smell!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: ...All I wanted was to help Jialiang find his missing wife as soon as possible, so that he could be on his way to the afterlife without any unfulfilled wishes making the journey more difficult than it needs to be...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Leave it to Bubu Pharmacy to snatch the perfect opportunity right outta my hands at the last hurdle! Never mind, I'll just have to put it down in the books as a deferred consideration.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: *sigh* One Qiqi was enough of a conundrum, the last thing I need's another one... If I'd known this was coming, I'd have whisked him off to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor the moment I found him...

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: Y—You stay away from my dad! When I grow up, I'm gonna become an even better doctor than Mom and Baizhu, and cure Dad for good!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Ooh, is that right? Well, you wouldn't be the first person who's tried to put Wangsheng Funeral Parlor out of business. If you're serious about it, you'll have your work cut out for you.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I'll catch you all another time!

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Phew... is she finally gone?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All's well that ends well! If you ask Paimon, we should probably do something to celebrate this hard-earned family reunion...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, at times like this, a grand celebratory feast is in order!

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Haha, it feels like it was a whole lifetime ago when I last talked with Jiangli and Ayu around the dinner table.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yaaay! Paimon can't wait!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, first things first, off to the market for some fresh ingredients! Let's goooo~!

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: Wait up! I'll come too!

response.speaker: Jiangli
response.text: Baizhu... Thank you so, so much for everything you've done for us.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Don't mention it, Jiangli. I was just doing my duty.

response.speaker: Jiangli
response.text: Just your duty, huh... Baizhu, Changsheng, would you mind if we took this conversation outside?

choices.text: Maybe I'll whip something up, too. It's been a while.
Paimon's idea of a celebration can only mean one thing...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Now that you are part-zombie, there are some rules that you need to know.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Uhh... Y—Yes, Ma'am. I'm listening...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: First. Don't forget to stretch your body regularly. Second. Don't forget to...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Yes? Go on? Don't forget to...?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: ...I forgot.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: ...I've taken a look at your Elixir of Immortality. It's not altogether dissimilar from the poison I concocted in terms of the way it functions.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...I have to say, Jiangli, it was a stroke of genius to use poison to maintain life. I hope you're not too upset at me for... copying your methods?

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: No, not at all. With your intellect, even if you'd never seen my poison, I believe you would have eventually arrived at the same approach.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: But I'm still impressed by how quickly you managed to gain such a thorough understanding of it. Jialiang's still only been in your care for a few days.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Not just that — you even managed to improve upon the original formula. That cannot be explained by intellect alone...

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Baizhu, be honest with me... Did you try out some of the poison on yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Hah! Told you the truth would surface sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: ...Life force isn't the only thing that Changsheng's contract lets you transfer between bodies, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Nothing gets past you, Jiangli.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: You are correct. Besides life force, Changsheng's secret art also allows for the transfer of toxins and diseases.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: When I treated Jialiang for the second time, I transferred some of the poison from his body into my own. Not only did this allow me to alleviate the burden on him, but it also gave me an opportunity to study its properties...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: There is no need to worry about any long-term consequences to my health, however. Now that the source has been destroyed, any remaining poison in me will have already dissipated.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: ...But you took such a huge risk. If we hadn't destroyed the gods' remains back there, then even you might have—

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: ...Hah. What am I saying? I'm in no position to criticize you for this.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: The reason I left our Master and went into hiding all those years ago was that he was getting old, and I didn't want him using up any more of his own life force to treat my husband.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: But in the end, how were my methods any different? I risked one life to save another. And then you tried the poison on yourself, too... It looks like both of us have ended up going the same way as our master before us.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Are all disciples of Chenyu Vale destined to turn out this way? To live a short life, having given away our own for the sake of others? To fight relentlessly against the natural course of life and death, whatever the cost? ...Maybe our fate is sealed the moment we decide to study medicine.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...We are doctors, Jiangli. We ought never say that anyone's fate is sealed.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Baizhu, I can tell that over the years, you've used the contract with Changsheng to transfer many diseases and toxins to yourself. There are so many, that some of them I don't even recognize...

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Can you... still stop before it's too late?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I think you know the answer, Jiangli. Every one of us from Chenyu Vale believes in the same thing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Food's ready!

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Mom! Come and join us!

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} taught me a load of new recipes, and said even dad'll be able to taste them! Come and try them out!

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Yes, darling, mom'll be there in just a second... Hey, slow down!

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: ...Baizhu, I know I won't be able to convince you, but... please don't forget that, if one day, you're not around anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Qiqi, Gui, and all the friends who have grown fond of you... they will all miss you dearly.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: There's no need to worry, Jiangli. I know what I'm doing.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I can only hope so.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Baizhu... What did Jiangli mean by "not around anymore"? Are you gonna be okay?

choices.text: Also, when Changsheng was talking about "fate"...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...Every single mortal I've ever contracted with, including Baizhu and Jiangli's Master, has passed away at a young age.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, that doesn't make any sense! You said that the contract with you helps people live longer!

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: *sigh* ...It is a very long story...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...My contract has strict requirements on the host's natural temperament. All my hosts have been most pure of heart.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: But when one with an altruistic nature gains access to this art, they are more seduced than the average person by the miracle of overturning the laws of life and death.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Though they know better than anyone else the fate that awaits them, when faced with the sorrows of humanity and the pain of losing their nearest and dearest, they cannot help but reach beyond human means.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...They are like moths that throw themselves into the flame, seeking a glimmer of hope in a dark world filled with pain and suffering.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Baizhu, does that mean...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Heh... I suppose that would make me a moth that yearns for the light, but doesn't want to be burned to a crisp.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Changsheng's art can transfer pain and suffering between people, but it cannot reduce the total amount of pain in the world. It's just like we witnessed: either Jialiang feared for Jiangli's life, or Jiangli grieved over Jialiang's sacrifice.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: I have nothing but the utmost respect for my predecessors who sacrificed their lives for their principles, but I do not wish to join their ranks... nor do I wish to pass on this contract to anyone else in the future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But, didn't you already transfer a ton of diseases onto yourself?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: What makes a poison, "poison"? And what makes a disease, a "disease"? When it comes down to it, are not both mechanisms that affect the operations of the human body?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: If disease is defined as deviation from normal functioning, then who knows... perhaps the true Elixir of Immortality could in fact be a kind of poison?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Many may view the notion of searching for immortality in poisons and illnesses as a flagrant violation of the natural order. But to me, it is no different from the way our ancestors tested the medicinal qualities of herbs by sampling each and every one.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: I don't want those who come after me to lose their lives to this contract, nor do I wish for Changsheng to perish from losing her host... This leaves only one solution, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Elixir of Immortality...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You have to become immortal yourself...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Precisely. I will be Changsheng's final host, and the tradition of passing down the contract will end with me.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...Even the gods of old struggled to achieve true immortality. First you want to save others, then you want to save yourself. Now you even want to save me... You're getting greedy, Baizhu.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Mmm... but isn't wanting to have it all what makes us human?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...For a selfish moth like me, who's afraid of the flame, yet yearns for the light, the only path forward is up towards the moon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh*... For once, Paimon just does not know what to say.

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: #Dr. Baizhu! {NICKNAME}! What are you still chatting about? The food's about to get cold!

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: We also have coconut milk, for Changsheng and Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ummm... Okay fine, let's go grab some food! Paimon has a bunch of burning questions, but they can wait till after we've eaten.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Ah, I do envy Paimon sometimes. Eating her fill is enough to satisfy her body and mind...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Hehe, true. And yet... although we call them simple pleasures...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Are such things as these not precisely why we mortals cling desperately to the life we have?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Jiangli's still waiting for us. Let's go talk to her, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: ...I feel a dull ache in my heart... This must be the way.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: This place feels familiar... I think I've been here before.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: I can feel it... We're getting close...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: We're almost there... It's right up ahead, the place where we made a pact together to... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Time flies... It's been so long since we bade each other farewell in Chenyu Vale.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: Changsheng, you're the same as ever. You haven't changed one bit!

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: You, on the other hand, have changed a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: ...You're right. My younger self would have never imagined that things would one day turn out this way.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangli
dialogues.text: ...Or that you'd turn out this way, Baizhu.
